tone_patterns: Formal, assurance-oriented tone that emphasizes oversight, accountability, and decision-making authority
Uses institutional voice (e.g., “the Group/Board/Committee”) rather than individual voice; individuals appear only in structured profile contexts
Balances principle-led statements (values/ethos) with operational governance mechanics (committees, roles, review cadence)
Employs cautious, compliance-aligned phrasing that signals alignment with broader reporting and governance documentation
paragraph_patterns: Opens with a high-level framing paragraph linking sustainability to business model and operations (capital, operations, products, stakeholder engagement)
Transitions from purpose/ethos to governance mechanism (who manages, how oversight is structured, what it enables)
Includes a cross-reference paragraph pointing readers to other corporate reports for the full governance picture
Uses a short “this report covers…” paragraph to preview what governance content will be explained (governance, risks/opportunities, strategy, metrics/targets)
Introduces a figure with a forward reference sentence explaining what the diagram shows and why it matters
After visuals/tables, returns to narrative paragraphs that define responsibilities, authority, and review processes
heading_patterns: Section numbering uses a two-level hierarchy: main section number/title (e.g., “02 Governance”) followed by subsections (e.g., “2.1 Overview”)
Subsection headings are short and functional (e.g., “Overview”, “The role of…”) and align to IFRS-style disclosure topics
Headings appear as standalone lines with clear spacing before body text; subsections are sequentially numbered
Uses role-focused headings for governance disclosures (board role, committee role) to mirror governance pillars
table_patterns: Member profile table format with consistent columns: Member name, Position, Years of experience, Job/competency summary, Qualifications relevant to role
Table title placed directly above the table; title describes the table purpose (background/summary) rather than repeating the section heading
Cells contain short narrative snippets (multi-line) rather than bullet lists; competency and qualification fields are descriptive
Table supports governance credibility by linking committee composition to relevant expertise (without relying on performance claims)
A short label/caption near the table indicates what the table represents (e.g., committee member profile) and ties it to the subsection context
figure_or_diagram_patterns: Large governance structure diagram that maps decision-making and oversight across levels (board, executive, group heads, working teams, subsidiaries)
Diagram uses layered hierarchy with clear vertical grouping and horizontal segmentation (e.g., board vs executive vs operational lines)
Includes directional connectors with repeated relationship labels (e.g., “informs”, “leads”) to clarify information flow and accountability
Incorporates a “lines of defence” concept as a visual organizing device (e.g., 1st/2nd/3rd line) to frame risk governance
Figure caption includes figure number and a descriptive title explaining the diagram’s scope (governance + decision-making process)
Diagram mixes entity boxes (committees/functions) with role boxes (key leadership roles) to show both structure and accountability points
pdf_layout_patterns: Section divider page: large section number and title with minimal content to signal a new chapter
Two-page spread behavior: narrative overview on one page followed by a full-width figure on the next page
Repeated running header/footer elements: section name appears as a header; report title and page number appear in the footer area
Figure occupies substantial page real estate; caption placed adjacent to or below the figure; page retains consistent margins
Use of whitespace to separate narrative blocks from visuals; clear visual hierarchy between headings, body text, and captions
Table and narrative share the page with a clear anchor label (e.g., a small subheading near the table) to orient the reader
disclosure_language_patterns: Defines committee mandates in terms of scope (strategy, risk/opportunity management, policies/disclosures, product development oversight)
Describes cadence and formality of oversight (e.g., periodic discussions, agenda incorporation, quarterly/annual review cycles) without overpromising outcomes
Clarifies decision rights and escalation pathways (board as highest authority; committees with delegated authority)
Uses cross-document references to indicate completeness of governance information across multiple reports
evidence_presentation_patterns: Evidence is presented structurally (diagram + committee mandate narrative + member profile table) rather than through performance metrics
Credibility is supported by showing: (1) governance architecture, (2) formal responsibilities, (3) competency/qualification alignment
Uses explicit mapping of roles to responsibilities (board/committee/executive) to demonstrate oversight coverage
Employs figure numbering and table titling to create audit-friendly traceability within the document
section_specific_observations: Governance section follows an IFRS-aligned flow: overview → governance structure visualization → committee composition/mandate → board role → committee role headings
The governance diagram is introduced in narrative before it appears, helping readers interpret the visual
Committee mandate text is dense and comprehensive, covering strategy alignment, risk/opportunity oversight, approvals, and monitoring cadence
Member profile content is separated into a structured table to avoid interrupting the governance narrative
things_to_avoid_copying: Any organization-specific committee names, acronyms, or internal governance bodies
Any individual names, titles, biographies, years of experience, or qualifications
Any claims about being embedded in ethos, value creation, or positive impact phrased as in the source
Any references to specific other reports by title/year
Any specific review frequencies, incentive structures, or target categories described in the source
Any subsidiary names, business unit names, or internal function labels
content_specific_items_detected_and_excl: Company name and report title/year references
Named committees and acronyms unique to the organization
Specific experience-year figures and qualification details
Specific subsidiary and business unit references
Specific statements about net-zero pathway or other organization-specific pathways
